skill.name: prisma-postgres-setup
skill.description: Provision a Prisma Postgres database through the Management API, then configure and verify a local Prisma 7 project.
skill.summary: Provision Prisma Postgres and connect a local Prisma 7 project through a guided workflow.
skill.author: prisma

security_audit.summary: Ten static findings are confirmed: eight executable command spans and two operations involving secret-bearing environment files. Most alerts are Markdown, official Prisma URLs, placeholders, or standard local configuration. Contextual review found unsafe token handling and permanent project deletion, but no prompt injection or unrelated exfiltration.

remediation.issue: The workflow asks users to paste a workspace service token into chat.
remediation.suggestion: Require secure environment injection or a secret manager. Remove chat-based token collection and redact credentials from tool output and logs.

remediation.issue: Bearer tokens are expanded into curl command arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Use an HTTP client that passes headers without shell interpolation. Ensure the agent and tools redact authorization headers from logs and errors.

remediation.issue: Quota recovery can permanently delete a selected project and every database.
remediation.suggestion: Stop after listing projects. Require separate confirmation naming the project and affected databases, and never delete resources automatically.

remediation.issue: The database credential is appended to a plaintext environment file.
remediation.suggestion: Verify Git exclusion before writing, update DATABASE_URL without duplication, avoid printing the value, and apply restrictive file permissions.

remediation.issue: The workflow runs package, provisioning, migration, and verification commands.
remediation.suggestion: Show each command and its scope before execution. Obtain approval for mutations and pin dependency versions where practical.

content.user_title: Provision Prisma Postgres for Local Projects
content.value_statement: Manual database provisioning and Prisma 7 configuration require several coordinated API, dependency, and migration steps. This skill guides the complete setup and verification workflow.
actual_capabilities: Lists available Prisma Postgres regions and helps users select an available location.
Creates a Prisma project and default database through the Management API.
Creates optional named database connections for developers or environments.
Configures Prisma 7 dependencies, environment loading, schema files, and the PostgreSQL adapter.
Creates an initial migration or uses schema push only for explicit prototypes.
Runs a temporary connection check and provides Prisma Studio and Console access paths.
limitations: Requires Node.js 18 or newer, a Prisma workspace, and a workspace service token.
Targets new Prisma Postgres databases and local Prisma 7 projects.
Does not manage CI/CD preview databases or embedded multi-tenant provisioning.
Cloud creation, deletion, migrations, and package installation can modify remote and local resources.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up a New Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up Prisma Postgres for this Node.js project. Ask before creating cloud resources, changing files, installing packages, or running migrations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for an empty or early-stage project.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter Database
prompt_templates.prompt: Provision a Prisma Postgres database in my chosen available region. Configure Prisma 7, add a starter blog schema, then verify the connection.
prompt_templates.scenario: Guided setup with a starter data model.

prompt_templates.title: Preserve Existing Models
prompt_templates.prompt: Connect this existing Prisma 7 codebase to a new Prisma Postgres database. Preserve existing models and create an initial migration after my confirmation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate setup for a repository with a Prisma schema.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Controlled Provisioning Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this repository for Prisma 7 readiness, propose required changes, provision a development connection, migrate safely, and report every local and remote modification.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review with controlled provisioning and migration.

output_examples.input: Connect my existing Prisma models to a new database without replacing the schema.
output: Preserved the existing models and configured the new database connection.
Created migration history after confirmation and generated the Prisma client.
Verified connectivity, then removed the temporary test file.

output_examples.input: Provision a database, but stop before deleting anything.
output_examples.output: Database creation stopped when the workspace limit was reached. Existing projects were listed, and no deletion occurred.

best_practices: Use a short-lived service token and rotate it after setup.
Review region, project name, schema, and destructive actions before confirmation.
Keep environment files ignored and inspect migrations before applying them.
anti_patterns: Do not paste production credentials into source files or commit environment files.
Do not delete projects automatically when a workspace limit is reached.
Do not use schema push when migration history is required.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates a Prisma project, a default Postgres database, and optional named connections through the Management API.

faq.question: Can it work without a service token?
faq.answer: No. The Management API requires a workspace service token with access to the target workspace.

faq.question: How should credentials be supplied?
faq.answer: Use secure environment injection or a secret manager when available. Rotate the token after setup and never commit environment files.

faq.question: Can it connect an existing database?
faq.answer: This workflow targets newly provisioned Prisma Postgres databases. Use standard Prisma configuration for a database that is already connected.

faq.question: Can the workflow delete cloud resources?
faq.answer: Its quota recovery path can delete a selected project. Project deletion is permanent and should require separate explicit confirmation.

faq.question: Which Prisma version does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Prisma 7 with ESM output, a driver adapter, and connection configuration outside the Prisma schema.
